subtopic: Different Forms of the Equation of a Circle
stem: Find the equation of a circle with centre at origin and radius 3.
solution:
Standard equation of a circle is

\(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\)  here \(r = 3\)

\(\therefore\ x^{2} + y^{2} = 3^{2}\)

\(x^{2} + y^{2} = 9\) is the equation of circle.

subtopic: Different Forms of the Equation of a Circle
stem: Find the equation of the circle with \(A(2,\ -3)\) and \(B(-3,\ 5)\) as end points of its diameter.
solution:
By using the diameter form;

\(A(2,\ -3) \equiv (x_{1},\ y_{1})\) and \(B(-3,\ 5) \equiv (x_{2},\ y_{2})\) are the co-ordinates of the end points of a diameter of the circle.

\(\therefore\) by the diameter form, equation of the circle is

\((x - x_{1})(x - x_{2}) + (y - y_{1})(y - y_{2}) = 0\)

\(\therefore\ (x - 2)(x + 3) + (y + 3)(y - 5) = 0\)

\(\therefore\ x^{2} + x - 6 + y^{2} - 2y - 15 = 0\)

\(\therefore\ x^{2} + y^{2} + x - 2y - 21 = 0\)

subtopic: Different Forms of the Equation of a Circle
stem: Find the equation of circle touching the Y-axis at point \((0,\ 3)\) and whose Centre is at \((-3,\ 3)\).
solution:
The circle touches the Y-axis at point \((0,\ 3)\), and the centre is \((-3,\ 3)\) we get radius \(r = 3\)

By using centre radius form;

\((x - h)^{2} + (y - k)^{2} = r^{2}\)

\((x + 3)^{2} + (y - 3)^{2} = 9\)

\(x^{2} + 6x + 9 + y^{2} - 6y + 9 = 9\)

\(\therefore\ x^{2} + y^{2} + 6x - 6y + 9 = 0\) is the equation of the circle.
_note: Accompanied by Fig. 6.4 (circle tangent to the Y-axis at (0,3) with centre C(-3,3)); the figure is illustrative and the stem is answerable without it.

subtopic: Different Forms of the Equation of a Circle
stem: Find the equation of the circle whose centre is at \((3,\ -4)\) and the line \(3x - 4y - 5 = 0\) cuts the circle at A and B; where \(l(AB) = 6\).
solution:
centre of the circle \(C(h, k) = C(3,\ -4)\)

\(3x - 4y - 5 = 0\) cuts the circle at A and B.

\(l(AB) = 6\)

\(CM \perp AB\)

\(\therefore\ AM = BM = 3\)

CM = Length of perpendicular from centre on the line

\(= \left|\dfrac{3(3) - 4(-4) - 5}{\sqrt{(3)^{2} + (-4)^{2}}}\right|\)

\(= \left|\dfrac{9 + 16 - 5}{\sqrt{9 + 16}}\right|\)

\(= \left|\dfrac{20}{5}\right| = 4\)

From right angled triangle AMC

\(CA^{2} = CM^{2} + AM^{2}\)

\(= (4)^{2} + (3)^{2}\)

\(= 16 + 9 = 25\)

\(CA\) = radius of the circle = 5

By centre radius form equation of the circle.

\((x - 3)^{2} + (y + 4)^{2} = 5^{2}\)

\(x^{2} - 6x + 9 + y^{2} + 8y + 16 = 25\)

\(x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x + 8y = 0\)
_note: Solution straddles pages p-01 and p-02 (it begins on printed p.128 and completes at the top of printed p.129). Accompanied by Fig. 6.5; the figure is illustrative and the stem is answerable without it.

subtopic: General Equation of a Circle
stem: Prove that \(3x^{2} + 3y^{2} - 6x + 4y - 1 = 0\), represents a circle. Find its centre and radius.
solution:
Given equation is

\(3x^{2} + 3y^{2} - 6x + 4y - 1 = 0\)

dividing by 3, we get

\(x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x + \dfrac{4y}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3} = 0\) comparing this with

\(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\)

we get \(2g = -2\)  \(\therefore\ g = -1\)

\(2f = \dfrac{4}{3}\)  \(\therefore\ f = \dfrac{2}{3}\) and \(c = \dfrac{-1}{3}\)

\(g^{2} + f^{2} - c = (-1)^{2} + \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{2} - \dfrac{-1}{3}\)

\(= 1 + \dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{16}{9}\)

As \(\dfrac{16}{9} > 0\)  \(g^{2} + f^{2} - c > 0\)

\(\therefore\ 3x^{2} + 3y^{2} - 6x + 4y - 1 = 0\) represents a circle.

\(\therefore\) Centre of the circle \(= (-g,\ -f) = \left(1,\ \dfrac{-2}{3}\right)\)

Radius of circle \(r = \sqrt{(-g)^{2} + (-f)^{2} - c}\)

\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{9}} = \dfrac{4}{3}\)

subtopic: General Equation of a Circle
stem: Find the equation of the circle passing through the points \((5,\ -6)\), \((1,\ 2)\) and \((3,\ -4)\).
solution:
Conside \(P = (5,\ -6)\), \(Q = (1,\ 2)\), \(R = (3,\ -4)\)

Let the centre of the circle be at \(C(h,\ k)\)

\(\therefore\ r = CP = CQ = CR\) = radii of the same circle

Consider \(CP = CQ\)

\(\therefore\ CP^{2} = CQ^{2}\)

By using distance formula,

\((h - 5)^{2} + (k + 6)^{2} = (h - 1)^{2} + (k - 2)^{2}\)

\(\therefore\ h^{2} - 10h + 25 + k^{2} + 12k + 36 = h^{2} - 2h + 1 + k^{2} - 4k + 4\)

i.e \(-8h + 16k = -56\)

\(h - 2k = 7\)  ........ (I)

Now consider, \(CQ = CR\)  \(\therefore\ CQ^{2} = CR^{2}\)

\((h - 1)^{2} + (k - 2)^{2} = (h - 3)^{2} + (k + 4)^{2}\)

\(\therefore\ h^{2} - 2h + 1 + k^{2} - 4k + 4 = h^{2} - 6h + 9 + k^{2} + 8k + 16\)

i.e. \(4h - 12k = 20\)  \(\therefore\ h - 3k = 5\) ......... (II)

Now, subtracting (II) from I, we get,

\(k = 2\)

Substituting \(k = 2\) in (II) we get

\(h = 11\)  \(\therefore\ C = (11,\ 2)\)

Radius of the circle is

\(r = \left|CP\right| = \sqrt{(11 - 5)^{2} + (2 + 6)^{2}} = \sqrt{100} = 10\);

By using centre-radius form, equation of the circle is \((x - 11)^{2} + (y - 2)^{2} = 100\)

\(\therefore\ x^{2} - 22x + 121 + y^{2} - 4y + 4 = 100\)

\(\therefore\ x^{2} + y^{2} - 22x - 4y + 25 = 0\)
_note: Solution straddles pages p-03 and p-04 (it begins on printed p.130 and completes on printed p.131). Both halves transcribed here. The book prints "Conside" for "Consider" in the opening line of the solution; transcribed as printed. Accompanied by Fig. 6.6 (a circle with centre C(h,k) and points P, Q, R marked); illustrative only.

subtopic: General Equation of a Circle
stem: Show that the points \((5,\ 5)\), \((6,\ 4)\), \((-2,\ 4)\) and \((7,\ 1)\) are on the same circle; i.e. these points are concyclic.
solution:
[Textbook misprint, not answer-affecting: the substitution into equation (IV) is printed \(20 + c = 4(-2) - 8(1) = -8 + 8\), but the solution has just derived \(f = -1\), so the second term must read \(-8(-1)\). The book's own arithmetic on that same line already uses the correct value — it writes \(-8 + 8\), and \(+8\) is \(-8(-1)\), not \(-8(1)\) — so \(c = -20\) and every line downstream of it is right. Preserved as printed.]

Let, the equation of the circle be

\(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\)  ....... (I)

The circle passing through \((5,\ 5)\), \((6,\ 4)\), \((-2,\ 4)\)

\(\therefore\ 50 + 10g + 10f + c = 0\)  ....... (II)

\(\therefore\ 52 + 12g + 8f + c = 0\)  ....... (III)

\(\therefore\ 20 - 4g + 8f + c = 0\)  ....... (IV)

Now (III) \(-\) (IV) gives  \(32 + 16g = 0\)

\(\therefore\ 16g = -32\)  \(\therefore\ g = -2\)

Subtracting (II) from (III)

we get \(2 + 2g - 2f = 0\)  ..... (V)

substitute \(g = -2\) in equation (V)

\(2 + (-4) - 2f = 0\)  \(2 - 4 = 2f\)  \(\therefore\ f = -1\)

Now substitute \(g = -2\) and \(f = -1\) in eqn. (IV)

\(20 + c = 4(-2) - 8(1) = -8 + 8\)

\(20 + c = 0\)  \(\therefore\ c = -20\)

Now substituting \(g = -2\), \(f = -1\) and \(c = -20\) in equation (I) we get,

\(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x - 2y - 20 = 0\) .... (VI) is the equation of the circle passing through the points \((5,\ 5)\), \((6,\ 4)\) and \((-2,\ 4)\).

If \((7,\ 1)\) satisfies equation (VI), the four points are concyclic.

L.H.S. \(= (7)^{2} + (1)^{2} - 28 - 2 - 20\)

\(= 49 + 1 - 50 = 0 =\) R.H.S.

\(\therefore\) Thus, the point \((7,\ 1)\) satisfies the equation of circle.

\(\therefore\) The given points are concyclic .
_note: Printed misprint in the step evaluating c: the book writes \(20 + c = 4(-2) - 8(1) = -8 + 8\), but with \(f = -1\) the term should read \(-8(-1)\). The book's own arithmetic (\(-8 + 8\)) already reflects the correct value, so the printed final answer \(c = -20\) is right; only the intermediate expression carries the sign slip. Transcribed as printed, not repaired.
